help: AI assistants reflexively prefix comments with NOTE/IMPORTANT/CAREFUL/CRITICAL/TIP/HACK to signal importance. Real human code rarely does this; the label is decorative, not load-bearing. Strip the prefix and let the comment speak for itself, or delete the comment entirely if it adds nothing the next line doesn't already say.

AI generates section banners like `# ====== SECTION 1 ======` to visually segment code that should be split into functions or modules instead. The banner is a smell that the surrounding code is too long. Either delete the banner and let the code stand on its own, or extract the section into a named function.

message: AI hedge or self-reference leaked into a code comment.
help: `# Note: this assumes...` and `# As an AI, I cannot...` are AI hedging that escaped into source. Either capture the assumption as an assertion (`assert x is not None, ...`) and remove the comment, or document the real precondition in a docstring. AI self-references should never appear in shipped code.

AI assistants praise their own output in comments: 'Pythonic', 'idiomatic', 'elegant', 'clean code', 'robust', 'comprehensive'. These are vocabulary tells, not facts. Real code either is good or isn't; the comment doesn't change that. Strip the praise; if the comment has no other content, delete it.

message: Emoji in source code (comment, identifier, or operator position).
help: AI assistants sprinkle emojis into comments and identifiers (`# ✅ done`, `def hello_🎉():`) — a strong AI fingerprint. Emojis in string literals (CLI output, user-facing text) are not flagged; those are intentional UX. Remove the emoji from the comment; if the comment becomes empty, delete the line.

AI training data is saturated with marketing prose; LLMs reach for promotional words (comprehensive, leverage, seamless, delve, showcase) in code comments. Per Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing'. Strip the marketing copy; describe the mechanism.

Comments starting with 'Furthermore,' / 'Additionally,' / 'Moreover,' / 'Notably,' are essay-prose habits that escaped into code. Per Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing'. Code comments are one line; they don't need transition words. Delete the connector.

message: Multiple em-dashes (—) in a single comment — the #1 LLM punctuation tell.
help: LLMs love em-dashes (U+2014). 2+ em-dashes in a single comment is a strong AI signature. Per Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing'. Use periods, parentheses, or commas instead.

AI emits placeholder TODOs as filler. A TODO without a ticket ID, URL, or owner is forgettable. Either link an issue (`TODO(JIRA-123)`, `TODO: https://...`) or delete the comment. Python's todo-without-ticket rule covers .py via the legacy pack; this rule covers Rust/Go/JS/TS.

detect.pattern: (?i)^\s*(your code here|implement this|placeholder|fill in|stub|to be implemented|not implemented)

help: `// your code here` / `// implement this` / `// placeholder` are AI prompt-stub markers that escaped into the response. The function is incomplete. Implement the body or delete the function. Python's stub-comment rule covers .py via the legacy pack.

`// fast, reliable, and scalable` triplet rhythm is LLM training-reward shape. Comma+comma+and triplets are an AI signature. Per Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing' rule of three. Pick one adjective or drop the comment.

detect.pattern: (?i)\b(not just .* but|not .* but rather|rather than .* we|not merely .* but)\b

help: `// not just X, but Y` / `// rather than X, we Y` is LLM stylistic parallelism. Per Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing'. State what the code IS, drop the contrast.

message: Inflated print() — celebratory emoji + Success/Done vocab.
help: `print("✨ Successfully processed all items!")` is canonical AI output. Use logger.info or a plain status line: `logger.info('processed %d items', n)`. Strip the emoji and the vocab.

message: Docstring lexically restates the function signature — no new information.
help: `def calculate_total(items, tax): """Calculate the total for items with tax."""` adds no info the signature doesn't show. Either drop the docstring or say what the signature doesn't: preconditions, side effects, error contract.

message: Generic variable name (data/result/value/item) in a long function.
help: In a function body > 8 statements, names like `data`/`result`/`value`/`item`/`tmp` give the reader nothing. Pick names that say what the variable IS in this context.

message: Type annotation matches what Python infers from the literal.
help: `count: int = 5` / `name: str = "alice"` / `ok: bool = True` — drop the annotation; inference works. Annotate when the RHS isn't a literal of the type (e.g. `count: int = compute()`).

message: Comment restates the next code line.
help: `# Return the result` above `return result` is noise. Comments should say WHY, not WHAT. Delete; or rewrite to add information the code doesn't show.
